clue.text: Perhaps it's the sea could fill a small one, from west to east and north to south!

definitions.text: Perhaps it's the sea could fill a small one, from west to east and north to south!

parts.words: Perhaps it's the sea could fill a small one, from west to east and north to south!
parts.note: the three words ITS, THE and SEA stacked in a three-by-three block read the same along the rows and down the columns

explanation.surface: A seemingly mystical remark about the ocean filling something small and spreading in every compass direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Write ITS, THE, SEA one under another: the columns spell the same three words, so the phrase fills a small grid both across and down.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid of letters whose rows and columns spell identical words is exactly this kind of puzzle, here a three-by-three example.

clue.text: Swish chap with a remarkable talent

definitions.meaning: a swish is a hissing rush of air, a whooshing sound
an expert or prodigy, someone brilliant at something

explanation.surface: A smart, stylish fellow who also happens to be gifted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a rushing hiss of sound and, informally, a person of exceptional skill: two senses, two definitions.

clue.text: I exhibit ups and downs, so using ramp I feel queasy

indicators.note: feeling queasy means churned up, so the letters of these words are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone prone to mood swings admits a sloping ramp makes them feel sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queasy' rearranges RAMP plus I FEEL; 'so using' merely joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart shading hills and valleys literally displays the ups and downs of the land's surface, spoken here in the first person.

clue.text: Hammer-thrower wiping out rhinoceros and prey

indicators.note: wiping out suggests wrecking or destroying, so the letters of these two words are smashed and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An athlete from the hammer event goes on a rampage, wrecking a rhinoceros and other prey.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cooper was a British heavyweight boxer whose left hook was nicknamed ''Enry's 'Ammer'; he was knighted, so throwing his 'hammer' meant throwing that punch.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxer's famous left hook was called his hammer, so he is jokingly a thrower of it rather than a field athlete.

clue.text: Effect of groundswell generated by addendum to letter in quality press

indicators.note: the postscript is placed inside the pair of other pieces, between them

parts.note: U means upper-class, of good social quality
to press someone is to urge them
PS, postscript, is the note added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a popular groundswell sparked by a postscript in a quality paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quality press' looks like the broadsheets; U is the old label for upper-class usage, and 'press' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising swell of popular feeling produces a sudden increase or surge, which is what this word means.

clue.text: Grub Street ultimately a little radical

parts.note: to grub is to dig about, as a pig rootles in soil

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the final letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A hack writer from Grub Street turns out to be mildly politically radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub Street' was London's home of hack writers; here 'Grub' is a verb and only the last letter of Street counts. 'Radical' is in the botanical sense, belonging to a root.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical comes from Latin for root, so a small root is a little radical in the punning botanical sense.

clue.text: Upset, much the worse for wear, one's out for the count

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so in this across light the remaining letters are turned round
out here means left out, so the letters of the number word are dropped

parts.note: far gone means badly drunk or dilapidated
one is the number word, spelt out; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A boxer, upset and battered, with one fighter out for the count.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ONE from FARGONE leaves FARG, which 'Upset' turns into the German title.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the German noble title equivalent to a count, as in Graf Zeppelin.

clue.text: Overhaul partially antiferromagnetic coils

indicators.note: coils suggests winding back on itself, so the run is read backwards up the down light
partially means only part of the long word is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A physics engineer partially overhauls some magnetic coils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partially' takes TIFER from inside the long word and 'coils' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a ship or machine is to fit it out again, restoring and re-equipping it.

clue.text: Say divorce settlement is "more than enough"

parts.note: a settlement after divorce is money for the ex, the former spouse
ample means plentiful, more than sufficient

explanation.surface: Someone claims their divorce settlement is more than generous.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface 'is' is just a link; 'Say' sits at the start as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Say is used to introduce an instance, as in 'take a fruit, say an apple', which this phrase also does.

clue.text: Noble died horribly, trampled by a steer —— it's not really fair

indicators.note: in a down light, being trampled puts the scrambled letters underneath the other pieces

parts.note: a, as in fifty pence a head, means per
a steer is a castrated bull, an ox

indicators.note: horribly suggests a gruesome mess, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A grim scene: a nobleman trampled to death by a steer, which is hardly fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' meaning PER is as in 'ten pounds a head'. 'horribly' makes IDEBLONDE, and 'trampled by' puts it underneath in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means light-haired; hair bleached chemically is fair only by artifice, not naturally so.

clue.text: One psychiatrist not wanting to take tip from Artful Dodger

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: not wanting to take means refusing a letter, so it is dropped from the name

parts.note: Alfred Adler was a famous Austrian psychiatrist

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist refuses to take advice from the Artful Dodger, the pickpocket in Oliver Twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artful Dodger' reads as Dickens's pickpocket, but the words split: 'Artful' supplies A to remove and 'Dodger' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodger avoids work or duty, and a lazy shirker who avoids effort is just such a person.

clue.text: Represented going steady?

definitions.meaning: having had someone talk on your behalf, as through a spokesperson
already in a relationship, claimed by a partner

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both having had someone speak on your behalf and being already taken by a partner.

clue.text: Not quite all correct beer-fuddled Times solver neglected to use it?

indicators.note: fuddled means confused with drink, so the letters are muddled
not quite all of the word means its final letter is missing

parts.note: the multiplication sign is X

explanation.surface: A grumpy note that a beer-befuddled Times solver did not quite get it all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims ALL to AL, which 'fuddled' rearranges with CORRECT and BEER; then X for 'Times'.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain's outer layer handles thinking, so a solver who failed was jokingly not using their grey matter.

clue.text: I note strike-breaking during recess ——— reason given

indicators.note: during means within, so the strike group sits inside the recess word

parts.note: a bower is a shady recess or arbour

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so the two letters go inside the strike word

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply

explanation.surface: A union note about strike-breaking during a parliamentary recess, with a reason given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike-breaking' reads as crossing a picket line; 'breaking' makes RAINP, which 'during' places within the arbour word.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason, the faculty of thought, is mental capacity, the intellectual strength meant here.

clue.text: Sapper's son pricks further guilt

parts.note: a sapper is a soldier of the Royal Engineers, RE

indicators.note: pricks means pierces, so the letter goes into the other word

parts.note: further means more

explanation.surface: A military engineer's son feels further pangs of guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilt and contrition are the deep regret felt after doing wrong, a near-synonym pairing.

clue.text: "Grammar, rhetoric and logic", singular subject for medieval University quiz night?

definitions.meaning: the three lower liberal arts of medieval education

definitions.text: singular subject for medieval University quiz night?
definitions.meaning: the Latin singular of trivia, the stuff of pub quizzes, was a medieval course of study

explanation.surface: Listing classical arts, then joking about a quiz night at a medieval university.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval three-part foundation course was this; its plural lives on as quiz trivia, hence the singular joke.

clue.text: In back of bus, old male's raising Cain — and he won't get off!

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: M is short for male

indicators.note: raising lifts it up, so in this down light the name is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: An old man raises Cain at the back of a bus and refuses to get off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get off' looks like leaving the bus; it means getting off to sleep. 'raising' turns CAIN into NIAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who suffers from sleeplessness cannot drift off, which is what get off means in the sleeping sense.

clue.text: Bumps into the work of Robin Goodfellow?

definitions.meaning: Robin Goodfellow, or Puck, is a mischievous sprite, and his work is a sprite's deeds

explanation.surface: Someone stumbling into the mischief of Shakespeare's Puck.
explanation.definitionFit: Collides with is a plain synonym; the second reading splits the word into a little devil's deeds.

clue.text: Learned about washed out seaside resort

indicators.note: about means around, so the wise word goes round the pale word

parts.note: a learned person is a sage
wan means pale, washed out

explanation.surface: Someone learned of a seaside resort ruined by rain.
explanation.walkthrough: SWANAGE is a seaside town in Dorset, on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorset town is a traditional English holiday resort on the coast.

clue.text: Oily liquid responsible for malfunctioning of coolers

indicators.note: a malfunction means things not working properly, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: An oily liquid blamed for broken-down coolers.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an oily aromatic compound obtained from wood tar, used as an antiseptic.

clue.text: Loveless bonkers would cheat on hubbies

indicators.note: love is the tennis score nil, a round letter, so loveless means one of those letters is dropped

parts.note: cuckoo means crazy, bonkers
LD is a contraction of would, keeping only its last two letters

explanation.surface: Bonkers wives without love who would cheat on their husbands.
explanation.walkthrough: LD for 'would' is unusual: dictionaries list only 'd, so treat it as the word cut to its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive a husband by being unfaithful is to make him a betrayed spouse, which this verb means.

clue.text: Notices section —— of one's own spine?

definitions.meaning: the part of a newspaper carrying private messages and small ads
belonging to oneself plus the backbone, the spinal stack

explanation.definitionFit: The newspaper page of private notices bears this name; read literally it would be one's own backbone.

clue.text: A single, revolting approach

parts.note: in cricket a single is one run scored
people in revolt are up in arms, risen up

explanation.surface: A lone, disgusting approach to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like disgusting; it means rising up in rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: The period leading up to an event, or a bowler's approach to the crease, is called this.

clue.text: Can have trouble following judge

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the trouble word comes after the letter

parts.note: to ail is to trouble, afflict

explanation.surface: Someone getting into bother after a judge's ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is slang for prison, not the verb or a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: The can is informal slang for prison, a place where offenders are locked up.

clue.text: Native American hotel embroiled in intrigue in times gone by

indicators.note: embroiled in means caught up within, so the lodging word goes inside

parts.note: a web is a tangle of intrigue or deceit
an inn is a small hotel
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A tale of a hotel caught up in a plot long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winnebago, or Ho-Chunk, are a Native American people of Wisconsin and Nebraska.

clue.text: African means to reject baby born on April 1st?

indicators.note: rejecting throws back, so the star-sign word is turned round

parts.note: someone born under the sign of Aries, the Ram, is an Arian

explanation.surface: An African tradition for rejecting a baby born on April Fools' Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' is money, not method; April 1st falls under Aries, giving ARIAN reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The currency of Nigeria is the naira, so it is the means of payment there.

clue.text: Hitch, Master of Suspense directed it

definitions.meaning: to hitch is to tether or tie up with a cord
Alfred Hitchcock, the Master of Suspense, directed a 1948 thriller of this title

explanation.surface: Hitchcock, nicknamed Hitch, made a film; the clue invites naming it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hitch' reads as Hitchcock's nickname but is the verb meaning to tie up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tether something with cord is to tie it fast, and Hitchcock's 1948 strangling thriller carries the same name.

clue.text: Top drawer, yet dark writer?

parts.note: to top a list is to lead it
a pencil is a thing that draws

explanation.surface: A top-quality piece of furniture, though gloomy, or a sombre author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' looks like furniture; it is something that draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A graphite writing tool leaves a grey-black line, so it is jokingly a writer of dark marks.
